name: Clomipramine
route_note: Oral capsules; IV infusion available in some countries.

discovery.note: A 3-chloro analogue of imipramine with much stronger serotonin reuptake inhibition.

tagline: The most serotonergic tricyclic, long the reference drug for OCD
summary: Clomipramine is a chlorinated analogue of imipramine and the most serotonergic tricyclic antidepressant. It was used in Europe from the 1960s and became the first drug approved by the FDA specifically for obsessive-compulsive disorder in 1989.
mechanism: Clomipramine is a potent inhibitor of serotonin reuptake; its metabolite desmethylclomipramine mainly inhibits noradrenaline reuptake. The strong serotonergic action is thought to underlie its efficacy in OCD.
Like other tricyclics it blocks muscarinic, H1 and alpha-1 receptors and cardiac sodium channels, producing anticholinergic, sedative and cardiovascular effects.

history.title: European use
history.detail: Clomipramine is introduced in Europe as Anafranil in the mid-1960s.

history.title: OCD reports
history.detail: Spanish psychiatrists Fernández-Córdoba and López-Ibor report benefit in obsessional symptoms.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Anafranil for OCD, the first drug licensed for that indication in the US.

history.title: Paediatric OCD
history.detail: A multicentre controlled trial supports use in children and adolescents with OCD (labelled from age 10).

history.title: Suicidality warning
history.detail: Class boxed warning on suicidality in young people.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2C19, CYP1A2, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Clomipramine is listed on the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines for obsessive-compulsive disorder.
